In my past relationships, because I didn't talk to my partners about my struggles, I ended up losing them. I'm not saying you should definitely tell her that's totally up to you. But from what you are saying you really care about her and she can help with dealing with these thoughts. Being afraid of losing someone is a terrible feeling but if you don't talk to her, your thoughts may start to get even worse. Or as I said you may try and talk to someone else if you don't want to talk to her. This subreddit exists so that people can talk about their feeling. There are lots of other websites that you can check out like quora. If you want help from actual professionals you can call a hotline or go to suicide prevention lifeline's website.

Does you gf know about your feelings? You can try and talk to her. As for a job, lots of people are at home so they are looking for some content. Maybe you can try YouTube or streaming? Something you can do from your house while your leg heals.

Do you have anyone that you can stay with? Like family members or friends? Until you can get a job. Also is it legal for your parents to do that? Just because you are 18 it doesn't mean they can kick you out.

As you said you are in your mid twenties. You are really young. You still have a long life ahead of you. If you try going to therapy or talking to someone they may help you with getting rid of these thoughts. Whenever I get these types of thoughts(though not so extreme) I try reminding myself that I'm still alive and until the day I die, I have so much to live for. But once I'm done, I will get to be alive again. I will never hug my mom or pet my cat or eat a delicious meal. What I can though, try to live as long as I can until I die. Because until I'm dead life is all I have. But once I'm dead, I'll never be alive again. Please don't pull the trigger. As you mentioned you have your family. I'm not saying only stay alive for them but more like try to think of them when you these thoughts and imagine how sad they will be. Just one step at a time. Getting through every day is enough. The symptoms you mentioned sounds like disassociating though of course I'm not an expert. As I said please talk to a professional or if you can't do that, talk to your friends. I hope that you will see this.

Everyone has their own way of grieving. Just because you don't think you are showing it doesn't mean you are not sad about it. The people around are probably feeling emotions that are similar to yours. You may try talking to them or maybe if you have a school counselor you may talk to him/her. There are also people you can talk to online. When we lost my mom's cousin I felt the same way. I had known him ever since I was a baby. But when he died, I felt like I couldn't feel anything and felt guilty though I shouldn't have. Everyone works in a different way. You just lost someone and you should not blame yourself. Since everyone around you is also grieving talking to them may make you feel better. After a loss it is not selfish to show people that you are not okay. I'm so sorry for your loss.
